name: X (Twitter)
description: Let your AI work with X (formerly Twitter): read and search posts, your timeline, mentions, bookmarks, Lists and direct messages, look up accounts and followers, and publish posts, replies and quotes, like, repost and send DMs after your confirmation.
instructions:
## X (Twitter)
This connector works with an X account through the **X API v2** (`https://api.x.com/2`), as the user who authorizes it: accounts, posts (read, search, count, publish, reply, quote, delete), the home timeline, mentions, likes, reposts, bookmarks, followers and following, Lists and direct messages.

**Pricing: X API access is paid.** The X API is billed per use with prepaid credits; new developers get no free plan (the old Free, Basic and Pro subscriptions are closed to them). Reading a post, an account or a message costs credits, publishing a post costs more, and a post with a link much more; reads of your own data are cheaper when the account that authorizes the connector also owns the developer app, and the same object read twice in one UTC day is billed once. When the balance runs out, X refuses every call until credits are added. Buy credits and set a spending limit in the Developer Console (https://console.x.com); check current prices at https://docs.x.com/x-api/getting-started/pricing. Keep `max_results` small and use expansions only when needed: each object returned is billed.

**Setup (one-time, about 10 minutes)**
1. Open the X Developer Console at https://console.x.com, sign in with the X account that owns the app, and **Create App** (name, description, use case). Add credits under billing, or calls are refused.
2. Open the app's **User authentication settings** and click **Set up**: App permissions **Read and write and Direct message** (Read and write is enough without the DM tools); Type of App **Web App, Automated App or Bot** (a confidential client, which gets a client secret); **Callback URI** `https://cloud.anythingmcp.com/api/mcp-oauth/callback` on AnythingMCP Cloud, or `<your AnythingMCP URL>/api/mcp-oauth/callback` when you host AnythingMCP yourself (X compares it exactly, trailing slash included; for a local test use `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/...`, not `localhost`); a **Website URL**. Save.
3. Copy the **OAuth 2.0 Client ID** and **Client Secret** (shown once) into `X_CLIENT_ID` and `X_CLIENT_SECRET`. The API Key and Secret and the Bearer Token of the app are for other sign-in methods and are not used here.
4. Install the connector, click **Authorize with Provider** and allow access on X. The connector asks for `tweet.read`, `tweet.write`, `users.read`, `follows.read`, `follows.write`, `like.read`, `like.write`, `bookmark.read`, `bookmark.write`, `list.read`, `dm.read`, `dm.write` and `offline.access`. Access tokens last two hours and are renewed automatically with the refresh token (`offline.access`); each refresh token works once.

**Read-only or no DMs**: remove the `.write` scopes (or the `dm.` scopes) in the connector's OAuth settings, authorize again and switch off the tools that need them.

**Your user id first**: tools that act on your own account (home timeline, likes, reposts, bookmarks, follows) take `user_id`, which is the numeric id from `x_get_me`, not the @username. `x_get_user_by_username` turns any @username into its id.

**Confirm first**: `x_create_post`, `x_reply_to_post`, `x_quote_post`, `x_repost`, `x_send_dm` and `x_send_dm_to_conversation` publish or deliver at once and cannot be taken back quietly. Show the user the exact text and the target, and wait for a yes. `x_follow_user` and `x_unfollow_user` notify or affect other people; confirm them too. `x_delete_post` and `x_delete_dm` are installed switched off.

**Replies**: X refuses API replies to posts whose author did not mention or quote the replying account (403), to keep automated replies out. Replying in your own threads and to mentions works.

**Fields and expansions**: X returns only `id` and `text` unless fields are asked for; every post tool asks for a useful default set (`tweet_fields`). Expansions (`author_id`, `referenced_tweets.id`, ...) put the related accounts and posts in `includes`, billed as extra reads. Long posts carry their full text in `note_tweet` (asked for by default); `text` holds only the first 280 characters. Lists use `meta.next_token`: pass it as `pagination_token` (`next_token` for searches) for the next page.

**Partial answers**: lookups by several ids or usernames answer 200 with `data` for what was found and `errors` (e.g. resource-not-found, not-authorized-for-resource) for the rest.

**Search** covers the last 7 days (`x_search_recent_posts`, `x_count_recent_posts`); queries are limited to 512 characters, and keyword searches no longer return reposts. Operators: `from:`, `to:`, `@mention`, `#hashtag`, `"exact phrase"`, `-term`, `lang:en`, `is:retweet`, `is:reply`, `has:links`, `has:media`, `url:`, `conversation_id:`.

**Direct messages** cover the last 30 days of regular DMs; encrypted conversations are not available through the API.

**Common errors**
- 401: the token was revoked or the app's secret changed; authorize again.
- 403 with `client-forbidden` or `client-not-enrolled`, or 429 `UsageCapExceeded` naming an old product such as standard-basic: the app is not on pay-per-use. In the Developer Console open the app, **Move to package** → **Pay-per-use** and put it in the **Production** environment (or create a new app), and make sure there are credits. 403 on a write: a missing scope or app permission (authorize again after changing it), a reply X does not allow, a duplicate post, or a DM the recipient does not accept.
- Every call failing after it worked before: the credit balance or the spending limit is used up; add credits or raise the limit.
- 429: rate limit per 15 minutes (per user and per app) or the monthly read cap; `x-rate-limit-reset` says when it resets. Wait and try again.

**Out of scope here**: media upload (posts are text or polls), the full-archive search, streams, Spaces, Communities, List and account management (create Lists, mute, block) and ads.

X_CLIENT_ID.label: OAuth 2.0 Client ID
X_CLIENT_ID.help: X Developer Console → your app → Keys and tokens → OAuth 2.0 Client ID and Client Secret: Client ID. Not the API Key.
X_CLIENT_ID.patternMessage: Paste the Client ID without spaces.

X_CLIENT_SECRET.label: OAuth 2.0 Client Secret
X_CLIENT_SECRET.help: Same place: Client Secret. Shown once; regenerate it if lost (the connector then needs a new authorization).
X_CLIENT_SECRET.patternMessage: Paste the Client Secret without spaces.

verifyHints.401: X refused the access token. Click Authorize with Provider again; if the Client Secret was regenerated, update X_CLIENT_SECRET first.
verifyHints.402: The X API credit balance or spending limit is used up. Add credits or raise the limit in the X Developer Console, then try again.
verifyHints.403: X refused the call. client-forbidden or client-not-enrolled means the app has no pay-per-use API access: in the X Developer Console (https://console.x.com) move the app to the Pay-per-use package and the Production environment, and add credits. On a write it can also mean a missing scope or app permission (set Read and write, authorize again).
verifyHints.rate_limited: X is rate limiting this user or app (limits reset every 15 minutes), or the monthly read cap is reached. Wait and try again.

prerequisites: An X account with an app in the X Developer Console (https://console.x.com) that has prepaid API credits, User authentication set up as a Web App with the callback URL below, and Read and write (plus Direct message) permission. X bills every read and post. About 10 minutes.

post_id.description: The id of the post to repost.

tools.name: x_undo_repost
tools.description: Take back your repost of a post; the original post stays. Answers retweeted: false.

user_id.description: Your own user id (the id from x_get_me, not the @username).

post_id.description: The id of the original post (not of your repost).

tools.name: x_list_bookmarks
tools.description: List your bookmarked posts, most recently bookmarked first (up to the last 800).

user_id.description: Your own user id (the id from x_get_me, not the @username).

max_results.description: Posts per page, 1 to 100 (default 10). Every post returned is billed as a read, so ask for what you need.

pagination_token.description: meta.next_token of the previous page, for the next one.

tweet_fields.description: Comma-separated post fields to return. Values: attachments, author_id, context_annotations, conversation_id, created_at, edit_controls, entities, geo, id, in_reply_to_user_id, lang, note_tweet (full text of long posts), possibly_sensitive, public_metrics, referenced_tweets, reply_settings, source, text, withheld; non_public_metrics and organic_metrics only for your own posts of the last 30 days. Default: created_at,author_id,conversation_id,in_reply_to_user_id,referenced_tweets,public_metrics,lang,entities,reply_settings,note_tweet.

expansions.description: Optional comma-separated expansions; the expanded objects come back in includes and are billed as extra reads. Values: author_id, referenced_tweets.id, in_reply_to_user_id, attachments.media_keys, attachments.poll_ids, entities.mentions.username, geo.place_id. Leave empty to keep the call cheap.

user_fields.description: Comma-separated user fields to return for expanded users (with expansions author_id and similar). Values: created_at, description, entities, id, location, name, profile_image_url, protected, public_metrics, url, username, verified, verified_type, withheld. Default: created_at,description,location,public_metrics,verified,verified_type,profile_image_url,url,protected.

tools.name: x_add_bookmark
tools.description: Bookmark a post. Bookmarks are private. Answers bookmarked: true.

user_id.description: Your own user id (the id from x_get_me, not the @username).

post_id.description: The id of the post to bookmark.

tools.name: x_remove_bookmark
tools.description: Remove a post from your bookmarks. Answers bookmarked: false.

user_id.description: Your own user id (the id from x_get_me, not the @username).

post_id.description: The id of the bookmarked post.

tools.name: x_list_followers
tools.description: List the accounts that follow an account, newest follower first. Each account returned is billed as a read: keep max_results small for large accounts.

max_results.description: Accounts per page, 1 to 1000 (default 20). Every account returned is billed as a read, so ask for what you need.

pagination_token.description: meta.next_token of the previous page, for the next one.

user_fields.description: Comma-separated user fields to return. Values: created_at, description, entities, id, location, name, profile_image_url, protected, public_metrics, url, username, verified, verified_type, withheld. Default: created_at,description,location,public_metrics,verified,verified_type,profile_image_url,url,protected.

tools.name: x_list_following
tools.description: List the accounts an account follows, most recently followed first.

max_results.description: Accounts per page, 1 to 1000 (default 20). Every account returned is billed as a read, so ask for what you need.

pagination_token.description: meta.next_token of the previous page, for the next one.

user_fields.description: Comma-separated user fields to return. tools.name: x_follow_user
tools.description: Follow an account as the authorized account; the other account is notified. Confirm with the user first. For a protected account this sends a follow request (pending_follow: true).

user_id.description: Your own user id (the id from x_get_me, not the @username).

target_user_id.description: The numeric id of the account to follow.

tools.name: x_unfollow_user
tools.description: Stop following an account as the authorized account. Confirm with the user first.

user_id.description: Your own user id (the id from x_get_me, not the @username).

target_user_id.description: The numeric id of the account to unfollow.

tools.name: x_list_owned_lists

user_id.description: The numeric user id; your own from x_get_me for your Lists.

max_results.description: Lists per page, 1 to 100 (default 20). Every list returned is billed as a read, so ask for what you need.

pagination_token.description: meta.next_token of the previous page, for the next one.

list_fields.description: Comma-separated list fields to return. Values: created_at, description, follower_count, id, member_count, name, private. Default: created_at,description,follower_count,member_count,private.

tools.name: x_list_followed_lists
tools.description: List the X Lists an account follows: id, name, description, member and follower counts.

max_results.description: Lists per page, 1 to 100 (default 20). Every list returned is billed as a read, so ask for what you need.

pagination_token.description: meta.next_token of the previous page, for the next one.

list_fields.description: Comma-separated list fields to return. Values: created_at, description, follower_count, id, member_count, name, private. Default: created_at,description,follower_count,member_count,private.

tools.name: x_get_list
tools.description: Read one X List: name, description, member and follower counts, whether it is private and when it was created.

list_fields.description: Comma-separated list fields to return. Values: created_at, description, follower_count, id, member_count, name, private. Default: created_at,description,follower_count,member_count,private.

tools.name: x_list_list_members

max_results.description: Accounts per page, 1 to 100 (default 20). Every account returned is billed as a read, so ask for what you need.

tools.name: x_list_dm_events
tools.description: List your recent direct messages across all conversations (the last 30 days), newest first. Needs the app permission Read, write and Direct messages.

event_types.description: Comma-separated event types: MessageCreate, ParticipantsJoin, ParticipantsLeave. Default: MessageCreate (messages only).

max_results.description: Messages per page, 1 to 100 (default 20). Every message returned is billed as a read, so ask for what you need.

pagination_token.description: meta.next_token of the previous page, for the next one.

dm_event_fields.description: Comma-separated message fields. Values: attachments, created_at, dm_conversation_id, entities, event_type, id, text. Default: id,text,event_type,created_at,dm_conversation_id,attachments.

expansions.description: Comma-separated expansions. sender_id (default) adds the sender to each message and the sender accounts to includes.users; also participant_ids and attachments.media_keys.

user_fields.description: Comma-separated user fields to return for the expanded senders. Values: created_at, description, entities, id, location, name, profile_image_url, protected, public_metrics, url, username, verified, verified_type, withheld. Default: created_at,description,location,public_metrics,verified,verified_type,profile_image_url,url,protected.

tools.name: x_list_dm_conversation_with_user
tools.description: Read your one-to-one direct message conversation with another account (the last 30 days), newest first.

participant_id.description: The numeric user id of the other account.

event_types.description: Comma-separated event types: MessageCreate, ParticipantsJoin, ParticipantsLeave. Default: MessageCreate (messages only).

max_results.description: Messages per page, 1 to 100 (default 20). Every message returned is billed as a read, so ask for what you need.

pagination_token.description: meta.next_token of the previous page, for the next one.

dm_event_fields.description: Comma-separated message fields. Values: attachments, created_at, dm_conversation_id, entities, event_type, id, text. Default: id,text,event_type,created_at,dm_conversation_id,attachments.

expansions.description: Comma-separated expansions. sender_id (default) adds the sender to each message and the sender accounts to includes.users; also participant_ids and attachments.media_keys.

user_fields.description: Comma-separated user fields to return for the expanded senders. Values: created_at, description, entities, id, location, name, profile_image_url, protected, public_metrics, url, username, verified, verified_type, withheld. Default: created_at,description,location,public_metrics,verified,verified_type,profile_image_url,url,protected.

tools.name: x_send_dm
tools.description: Send a direct message to an account, in your one-to-one conversation with it (created when needed). The recipient sees it at once: show the user the exact text and get a yes first. Fails with 403 when the recipient does not accept messages from you.

participant_id.description: The numeric user id of the recipient.

tools.name: x_send_dm_to_conversation
tools.description: Send a direct message into an existing conversation (one-to-one or group) by its dm_conversation_id from x_list_dm_events. Everyone in it sees it at once: show the user the exact text and get a yes first.

dm_conversation_id.description: The conversation id, e.g. 123-456 for one-to-one or a number for a group.

tools.name: x_delete_dm
tools.description: Delete one of your direct messages, for you only (the other side keeps it). Installed switched off; confirm with the user first.

event_id.description: The id of the message event.
